run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:34:46Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is the downstream edge of a failure in the ad workload. frontend-proxy's own error spans (span_name=ingress and router frontend egress) rose from ~0.005/s at 17:34:46 to 0.869/s at 17:44:46, and its access log shows 500 responses with 'via_upstream' only for GET /api/data requests, i.e. the 500s are produced by the frontend upstream, not by the proxy. The frontend's own error spans are confined to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and its parents (executing api route (pages) /api/data, GET /api/data, GET); by 17:45 those spans are 100% STATUS_CODE_ERROR. The ad pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 had its ad container OOMKilled (exit 137) at 17:34:15Z after its working set climbed from ~310MB to 420MB against a 450Mi limit; the replacement container started at 17:34:16Z, has since been CPU-throttled in ~99.9-100% of CFS periods against a 50m CPU limit, and emits no GetAds server spans after ~17:35 (rate 1.7-2.2/s -> 0) and no log lines after 17:34:12Z. Because the ad container defines no readiness/liveness/startup probe, the pod and Deployment still report Ready/Available. Checked entities that are not failing on their own evidence: frontend-proxy pod and frontend pod both Running with restartCount 0 and flat memory; no new error series appeared for checkout, payment, accounting or other operations. A separate fraud-detection OOM restart at 17:11:47 was checked and rejected as a cause.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error signal matches the alert: sum by (span_name,status_code) rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}) shows ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.00526/s at 17:34:46 rising to 0.6807/s at 17:40:46 and 0.8688/s at 17:44:46, and 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0/s until 17:34:46 rising to 0.8654/s at 17:44:46, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET volume stayed roughly flat at 9.7-11.4/s.

frontend-proxy access logs show the failing responses are 500 '- via_upstream' with a 21-byte body for GET /api/data?contextKeys=... (all contextKeys variants), while GET /api/products/..., GET /api/cart, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and GET / returned 200 (and /api/data/ returned 308 redirects) in the same period.

Among all services, the only new error spans in the window are frontend and frontend-proxy: frontend errors are localized to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, executing api route (pages) /api/data, GET /api/data, GET and tcp.connect; checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and PaymentService/Charge, payment grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and accounting 'orders receive' all read 0.

The frontend's GetAds and GET /api/data spans became fully failed: at 17:45:00 both had STATUS_CODE_ERROR 1.0067/s and STATUS_CODE_UNSET 0, whereas at 17:27-17:33 GetAds ERROR was 0 and UNSET was ~1.24-1.30/s and GET /api/data ERROR was 0 with UNSET ~1.24-1.30/s; the first nonzero error values appear in the 2-minute window ending 17:36:00.

The ad service stopped serving GetAds: with a 1-minute rate, service_name=ad span_name=oteldemo.AdService/GetAds is ~1.67-2.17/s through 17:35:00, then 0 at every sample from 17:36:00 to 17:44:00; the 10-minute view shows the same decline (0.8702/s at 17:32:46 to 0 at 17:44:46).

Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 (namespace otel-demo) has ad container lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 16:57:14Z, finishedAt 17:34:15Z; restartCount 1; current state running with startedAt 17:34:16Z and ready true.
The ad container's declared resources are limits cpu 50m and memory 450Mi (requests 10m/225Mi) and it defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe.

The pre-restart ad container's working set was ~301-310MB through 17:33:00, then 333.9MB at 17:34:00 and 420.4MB in its last sample; the replacement container (container id ed742b6451d6...) climbed from 65.6MB at 17:35:00 to peaks of 354MB (17:40) and 373MB (17:43), under the 450Mi limit.

The ad container's CPU throttling ratio (rate of container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total / container_cpu_cfs_periods_total) was ~0.10-0.16 up to 17:33, then 0.5217 at 17:35, 0.8440 at 17:37, 0.9996 at 17:39 and 0.9993-1.0 from 17:41 through 17:45.

The newest log line returned for the ad container is 2026-11-16T17:34:12.817405Z ('Targeted ad request received for [accessories]'); no log lines from the instance that started at 17:34:16Z were returned (previous-instance stream unavailable, HTTP 400 'previous terminated container not found').

The only Kubernetes events in namespace otel-demo inside the window are Normal Pulled, Created and Started for pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 around 17:34:15-17:34:16Z, consistent with a container restart; no Evicted or node-pressure event was observed.

The ad Service (clusterIP 100.64.156.55, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad) has an endpoint address 100.96.4.112 with targetRef Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25, and the pod carries label opentelemetry.io/name=ad, so service-to-pod routing/selection is not the mismatch.

Deployment ad (and Deployment frontend) in otel-demo report replicas 1, ready 1, available 1; Deployment ad's Available condition has lastTransitionTime 2026-11-16T17:34:16Z, i.e. it flipped at the container restart and its Ready status is not a serving signal because the ad container has no probes.

frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-whhck and frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-cmhqq are both phase Running with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and their container working sets are flat (frontend-proxy ~20.4MB, frontend ~129MB) across 17:10-17:46.

The trigger of the outage is memory-limit exhaustion on the ad container: its working set rose from ~310MB to 420MB against the 450Mi limit in the final minutes before the kubelet OOMKilled it (exit 137) at 17:34:15Z, which removed ad's GetAds capacity and started the frontend/proxy 500 cascade about 30 seconds before the alert.

The reason ad has not recovered after the restart is CPU starvation of the replacement container: with a 50m CPU limit its CFS throttled-period ratio reached ~0.999-1.0 from 17:39 onward, and in the same period it emitted no GetAds server spans and no log lines, while the pod still reports Ready because no readiness probe exists.

frontend-proxy being the origin of the errors was considered and rejected: its container is running with restartCount 0 and flat ~20MB memory, and the failing responses it logs are 500 'via_upstream' carrying the frontend's response, so the proxy is relaying an upstream 500 rather than generating it.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (container lastState terminated OOMKilled exitCode 137 at 17:11:47Z, restartCount 1) was considered as a contributing cause and rejected for this alert: it precedes the frontend/proxy error onset by ~23 minutes, checkout PlaceOrder and PaymentService/Charge error rates stayed at 0, and fraud-detection's only error series is a pre-existing flagd EventStream baseline of ~0.0017-0.0019/s.

The error rise is not explained by a traffic surge: frontend-proxy ingress span volume (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) stayed between about 9.70/s and 11.46/s across 17:10:46-17:44:46 while the error rate went from ~0 to 0.87/s.

Give the ad container headroom and a real start-up gate: raise its memory limit above the observed 420MB working set (or reduce heap via JVM settings), raise the 50m CPU limit so a restarted JVM can initialize instead of being throttled ~100% of periods, and add readiness/liveness probes so a non-serving instance is not reported Ready (configuration changes only; not executed here).

Verify on the human side whether the ad container eventually finishes starting or crash-loops again (watch restartCount, container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total and ad GetAds spans); a rollout/restart of Deployment ad with adequate limits would be the operational recovery step, but no remediation is authorized or performed in this investigation.

gaps: The frontend application produced no log lines at all (both instances read 0 bytes), so the exact gRPC error code/message behind grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds errors (e.g. UNAVAILABLE vs DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) is unverified.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend, ad or frontend-proxy in the windows queried (backend_traces_returned 0), consistent with its most-recent-5000-traces retention, so span-level error details for this incident are unknown.
rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count had no series for frontend or frontend-proxy in the window, so a gRPC status-code breakdown of the failing GetAds calls is unavailable.

No log lines from the post-17:34:16Z ad container were retrievable (previous instance also unavailable, HTTP 400), so whether the new JVM is still starting, blocked, or unable to write logs is unresolved.

Querying {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned no data, so kube-state-metrics pod/container status series (e.g. ready/terminated-reason gauges) could not corroborate the pod state; only cAdvisor container metrics were available.
The RequestErrorRate alerting rule named in the alert was not found via list_prometheus_rules (no_data), so the rule expression, threshold and evaluation labels could not be verified.
The change_history integration is not available, so whether the ad container's resource limits were changed recently cannot be checked.

Impact outside the /api/data path was not established: error series were absent for other frontend routes and for cart/product-catalog/recommendation/shipping/currency/email, but an absent series is unknown rather than proof of zero errors, so their health is not certified.
next_steps: Check the ad container's current restart count and memory/CPU throttling again (container_memory_working_set_bytes, container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) to see whether it converged or is still starved.
Review Deployment ad's resource limits (memory 450Mi, cpu 50m) against actual JVM heap needs and add readiness/liveness probes.
Alert on ad service availability directly (GetAds server span rate or a readiness-based signal) because the pod/Deployment Ready state does not reflect ad's serving ability.
Confirm the exact frontend GetAds failure mode from frontend application logs once a logging source is available.
